title: ECDSA fd mutex serializes all sign/verify: throughput cliff for multi-session TLS servers
description:
Scenario: A TLS server handling N concurrent handshakes. Each TLS 1.3 handshake requires at least one ECDSA sign. All N sign operations queue behind g_ecdsa_fd_lock. This is serialized even if the hardware supports concurrent DO_SIGN ioctls on multiple fds.

The comment in the code acknowledges this: 'On a TLS server with many concurrent handshakes this can become a throughput bottleneck.'

The design is intentional (DO_SIGN/DO_VERIFY were verified only on the global fd). But this becomes a support issue the moment someone benchmarks the port on a loaded server. They will file a performance issue, it will look like a hardware bottleneck, and the root cause is the single-fd serialization.

Maintenance consequence: Performance complaint with non-obvious root cause. The comment naming this bottleneck is the current mitigation.

Leaving a tracked issue here so the future-me who pools ECDSA fds has the context.
